findings.title: _get_price is a 1,933-line method inside the module CLAUDE.md calls "orchestrator only"
findings.claim: StructuredComparisonService._get_price spans lines 5044-6976 (1,933 lines) with 299 decision points, 32 return statements, 152 distinct assigned locals, 9 nested closures and a max block nesting depth of 6 — a single method larger than 63 of the repo's 68 service modules.
findings.evidence: AST measurement of the def at :5044 (end_lineno 6976). Nested closures at that scope: _ps_mark, _cancel_prefetched_discovery, _cancel_prefetched_direct, _consume_adapter_prefetch, _consume_bound, _suppl_reject, _maybe_park_supplement, _finalize_fan_winner, _page_scrape_supplement_stage. Second-largest in the same file is _fetch_product_data at :4168 (660 lines); the two together are 34% of the 7,563-line file.
findings.failure_scenario: COST: any change to price resolution must be reasoned about across 299 branch points and 32 exit paths in one scope with 152 live locals. Concretely, the 2026-08-30 wave needed a module-reference-based regression gate (CLAUDE.md:521) precisely because no one can predict which of the 32 exits a change moves; the filename-keyword gate missed the one deterministic regression. A 1,933-line body is why that gate has to exist.
findings.fix_sketch: The 9 nested closures are already named seams. Lift them to module-level functions taking an explicit context object, which alone moves ~400 lines out and makes each independently testable; then split the supplement stage (_suppl_reject/_maybe_park_supplement/_page_scrape_supplement_stage) into a price_supplement_stage module the way noon/salla/occ adapters were already split out.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived by AST against the pinned tree. `ast.parse` of app/services/structured_comparison_service.py reports `_get_price` at lineno=5044, end_lineno=6976 => 1933 lines, 32 `ast.Return` nodes, 152 distinct Store-context Name bindings, and exactly the 9 nested closures named in the finding (_ps_mark, _cancel_prefetched_discovery, _cancel_prefetched_direct, _consume_adapter_prefetch, _consume_bound, _suppl_reject, _maybe_park_supplement, _finalize_fan_winner, _page_scrape_supplement_stage). Two numbers drift slightly and neither changes the claim: my decision-point count is 318 (If/For/While/ExceptHandler/IfExp/Assert + BoolOp arms + comprehensions) vs the reported 299 -- a counting-rule difference, and larger, not smaller; and 64 of the 68 modules under app/services/ are shorter than 1933 lines, not 63 (glob+wc: extraction_service.py measures 2465). CLAUDE.md:107 verbatim: '`app/services/structured_comparison_service.py` (~1,500 lines, orchestrator only)'. wc -l = 7563.

findings.evidence: Zero-reference, verified individually: get_product_cache :637, set_product_cache :643, get_comparison_cache :649, set_comparison_cache :655, check_rate_limit :668, increment_user_daily_usage :698, track_api_cost :715, check_monthly_budget :730, plus the two key generators only those consume (get_product_cache_key :590, get_comparison_cache_key :602) and get_user_daily_usage :689 (called only by the dead check_rate_limit). The numeric divergence is REAL and is the load-bearing part: cache_service.py:665 `FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT = int(os.getenv("FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT", "5"))` consumed at :678 `daily_limit = FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT`, against usage_service.py:17-27 `TIER_LIMITS = {"free": {"lifetime_free": 3, "monthly": 10, "daily": 3}}`. 5 vs 3 confirmed. findings.title: serper_service exports 5 zero-reference functions (137 lines) that spend PAID Serper credits
findings.claim: Five public async/sync entry points in serper_service.py — search_product_price :453 (26 lines), search_product_specs :896 (24), search_product_reviews :922 (20), search_gcc_retailer_prices :1100 (23), extract_prices_from_text :1129 (44) — have zero references anywhere in app/, scripts/ or tests/, and four of them issue billable Serper calls.
findings.evidence: Every importer of the module was enumerated: image_service.py:42 takes search_images; price_service.py:32 and structured_comparison_service.py:41 take search_product_prices/search_price_organic/search_web; review_service.py:18 and scripts/research_goldtruth_seed.py:43 take search_web; rating_service.py:276 takes _clean_shopping_query. None of the five listed above is imported by anything. Note the near-collision: the LIVE function is `search_product_prices` (plural, :705); the dead one is `search_product_price` (singular, :453).
findings.failure_scenario: CONCRETE: a maintainer adding a price lookup greps `search_product_price`, finds the singular dead one first (it is 250 lines earlier in the file), and wires it. It is a bare /search call with none of the live path's protections — no _serper_budget_ok() gate, no key rotation via _active_serper_key, no _serper_rotation_deadline (:302, 14s, pinned under the 15s race). Result: unmetered credit burn on a key CLAUDE.md:193 prices at $0.001/call, plus a call that can stall past the price race with nothing to bound it.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete all five. If any is wanted later it must be rebuilt on _serper_post, which is where the budget gate, rotation and deadline live.
findings.verify_evidence: DEAD-CODE HALF CONFIRMED, DANGER NARRATIVE REFUTED. Confirmed: word-boundary grep across app/, scripts/, tests/ excluding serper_service.py returns 0 for all five -- search_product_price, search_product_specs, search_product_reviews, search_gcc_retailer_prices, extract_prices_from_text -- at the cited lines :453, :896, :922, :1100, :1129, totalling ~137 lines, and the singular/plural name collision with the live search_product_prices (:705) is real. REFUTED: the finding's P2 justification is that wiring the dead singular is 'a bare /search call with none of the live path's protections -- no _serper_budget_ok() gate, no key rotation via _active_serper_key, no _serper_rotation_deadline', causing 'unmetered credit burn'. I read the body. serper_service.py:470 is `results = await search_product_prices(product_name, code)` -- it DELEGATES to the live function, which carries `if not _active_serper_key()` at :723 and `if not _serper_budget_ok()` at :729, and reaches the network only via _serper_post (:330), where rotation and the 14s deadline live. The other three network functions delegate to search_web, whose identical gates sit at :507 and :517. extract_prices_from_text (:1129) is a pure regex helper that makes no network call at all, so 'four of them issue billable Serper calls' is true only in the sense that they issue fully budget-gated ones. Nothing here can burn an unmetered credit. What remains is 137 lines of genuinely unreferenced wrapper code plus a name-collision trap -- real, but bloat, not exposure. (Noted in passing, not claimed by the lane: search_videos :944 and search_news :1021 are also production-unreferenced, tests-only.)

findings.title: Three unused direct runtime dependencies ship to Railway on every deploy
findings.claim: lxml, tiktoken and pydantic-settings are declared as direct runtime dependencies but no deployed code imports them; removing the three drops 6 of the 69 locked runtime packages (8.7%).
findings.evidence: AST import inventory over app/, scripts/, tests/ and root: **lxml** — zero imports and zero `"lxml"` parser strings anywhere; all 14 BeautifulSoup call sites in app/ pass `"html.parser"` (11 double-quoted, 3 single-quoted). **tiktoken** — zero imports in app/; only scripts/audit_exemplar_token_cost.py:53, tests/test_exemplar_injection_content.py:53, tests/test_prompt_caching.py:7, i.e. dev-only. **pydantic-settings** — one importer, app/config.py:5, which CLAUDE.md:441 itself documents as dead-and-a-trap. Lock confirms all three are direct, not transitive: requirements.txt:93 `lxml==6.1.2  # via -r requirements.in`, :162 `tiktoken==0.14.0  # via -r requirements.in`, :121 `pydantic-settings==2.15.0  # via -r requirements.in`. Transitive fan-out: regex==2026.7.19 (:138 `# via tiktoken`), requests==2.34.2 (:140 `# via tiktoken`), charset-normalizer==3.5.1 (:27 `# via requests`) exist in the runtime lock SOLELY because of tiktoken. Counter-checked and NOT unused: python-multipart is required by app/api/image_routes.py:61 `List[UploadFile] = File(...)`, email-validator by the EmailStr fields at auth_routes.py:79/104/113 — both are implicit deps with no import statement.
findings.failure_scenario: COST: lxml 6.1.2 is a C-extension wheel built/installed on every NIXPACKS build; tiktoken drags in `requests` + `regex` + `charset-normalizer`, putting a second HTTP stack into the production image that no runtime code uses. That is 6 extra packages in the `pip-audit --strict` surface that CLAUDE.md:19 lists as an App-Store production gate — every future CVE in requests/urllib3/charset-normalizer/lxml becomes a release blocker for code that does not exist.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop `lxml` and `pydantic-settings` from requirements.in; move `tiktoken` to requirements-dev.in (it is genuinely used by scripts/audit_exemplar_token_cost.py and two tests). Recompile both locks with the uv command in the file header; CI's existing "Lock is current" step (.github/workflows/ci.yml:31) verifies the result.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived every leg. lxml: my own grep for `from lxml|import lxml|etree|soupparser|read_html|features=|'lxml'|"lxml"` across app/ and scripts/ returns exactly one hit and it is stdlib -- sitemap_discovery_service.py:62 `from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET`. All 14 BeautifulSoup call sites in app/ pass a parser string and every one is html.parser (11 double-quoted, 3 single-quoted, counted by regex extraction). tiktoken: zero imports in app/; dev-only consumers are scripts/audit_exemplar_token_cost.py:53, tests/test_exemplar_injection_content.py:53, tests/test_prompt_caching.py:7 and -- one the finding missed -- tests/test_specs_no_fabrication_guard.py:191 (a pytest.importorskip, so still dev-only; the conclusion is unchanged). pydantic-settings: single importer app/config.py:5, the module CLAUDE.md:441 documents as a trap. Lock re-read line by line: requirements.txt:93 lxml==6.1.2 '# via -r requirements.in', :162 tiktoken==0.14.0 '# via -r requirements.in', :121 pydantic-settings==2.15.0, :138-139 regex '# via tiktoken', :140-141 requests==2.34.2 '# via tiktoken' (tiktoken is its ONLY parent), :27 charset-normalizer '# via requests'. Runtime lock package count = 69 exactly, so 6/69 = 8.7% holds. Counter-check reproduced: no bare `import requests` anywhere -- the 20+ hits are `from curl_cffi import requests`, a different distribution. pip-audit --strict confirmed as an App Store production gate in CLAUDE.md's 'Routine before App Store production submission' line.

findings.title: pyproject.toml is a stale third dependency declaration that would install a non-bootable app
findings.claim: pyproject.toml [project].dependencies lists 15 packages against requirements.in's 18 and omits slowapi, sentry-sdk and tiktoken, so `pip install .` / `poetry install` produces an environment where `import app.main` raises ImportError — and no CI gate ties the two files together.
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml:9-25 lists fastapi, uvicorn, openai, httpx, supabase, redis, pydantic, pydantic-settings, python-dotenv, python-multipart, email-validator, upstash-redis, beautifulsoup4, lxml, curl-cffi. Missing vs requirements.in: slowapi (imported at app/main.py:38, app/middleware/error_handler.py:17, app/middleware/rate_limiter.py:4), sentry-sdk (app/middleware/error_handler.py:153, app/services/api_budget_service.py:446, app/services/database_service.py:189), tiktoken. [dependency-groups].dev at :30 lists only pytest/pytest-asyncio/black, omitting pytest-timeout, pip-audit, ruff, pillow, pytest-cov and sqlfluff — all six of which requirements-dev.in declares and CI installs. requirements.in:1 asserts "Runtime dependency SOURCE. Edit this file, never requirements.txt" but says nothing about pyproject. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:27) installs from requirements*.txt only; the "Lock is current" gate at :31 diffs requirements.in→txt and never reads pyproject.
findings.failure_scenario: CONCRETE: a contributor (or a container recipe, or any tool that treats pyproject as authoritative — Dependabot, Renovate, `uv sync`, an IDE) installs from pyproject and gets an app that dies at startup on `from slowapi import Limiter` (app/main.py:38). Railway is unaffected because NIXPACKS picks requirements.txt, which is exactly why this has stayed broken and undetected.
findings.fix_sketch: Either delete [project].dependencies + [dependency-groups] entirely (the file already sets `package-mode = false` at :34, so it is not a build input) leaving only the [tool.pytest]/[tool.ruff] config it genuinely owns; or add a CI step diffing the two lists. Deleting is cheaper and removes the third source of truth.
findings.verify_evidence: FACTS CONFIRMED, SEVERITY OVERSTATED. Confirmed by reading pyproject.toml with line numbers: [project].dependencies spans :9-25 and lists exactly the 15 packages named; requirements.in declares 18; the three missing are slowapi, sentry-sdk and tiktoken. The import sites are real -- `from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded` at app/main.py:38 and app/middleware/error_handler.py:17, `from slowapi import Limiter` at app/middleware/rate_limiter.py:4, `import sentry_sdk` at error_handler.py:153, api_budget_service.py:446, database_service.py:189 -- so an env built from pyproject alone does die at `import app.main`. [dependency-groups].dev lists 3 of the 9 entries requirements-dev.in declares (omitting pytest-timeout, pip-audit, ruff, pillow, pytest-cov, sqlfluff). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) installs `-r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt` and the 'Lock is current' step compiles only the .in->.txt pair, never reading pyproject. TWO LINE ERRORS: `package-mode = false` is at :48 under [tool.poetry], NOT :34; [dependency-groups] opens at :31, not :30. DOWNGRADED because the cost is entirely latent: `ls .github` shows only black-clean-paths.txt and workflows/{ci,live-suite}.yml -- there is NO dependabot.yml and NO renovate config in this tree, and neither NIXPACKS nor CI reads pyproject for dependencies. Every actor in the failure scenario (Dependabot, Renovate, uv sync, a contributor running `pip install .`) is hypothetical here. A real stale third manifest, worth deleting; not a P2 measurable cost today.

findings.title: 16 abandoned root-level files are tracked in git, and the .gitignore rules meant to cover them are inert
findings.claim: Sixteen scratch artifacts sit tracked at the repo root — 9 one-off .py probes, 6 result-dump .json blobs and a 53 KB binary .coverage database — untouched for 3 to 7 months, and .gitignore's `/test_*.py` and `response_*.json` rules cannot untrack the ones already committed.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files --error-unmatch` confirms all 16 are tracked: parse_live.py, parse_luxury.py, parse_result.py, phase0_gucci.py, phase0_lv.py, phase0_lv_curl.py (all last touched 2026-05-03), phase0_test.py (2026-06-20), test_client.py, test_services.py (2026-02-08), .coverage (2026-03-08), full_response.json, tmp_result.json, tmp_result2.json, session23_test_response.json, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_result.json, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_luxury_test.json (2026-05-03). The last two filenames are a Windows absolute path with separators stripped — a shell-redirect accident that got committed. .gitignore:33 `/test_*.py` and :31 `response_*.json` were added to stop exactly this class, but git ignore rules never apply to already-tracked paths, so test_client.py and test_services.py remain tracked and `full_response.json` does not even match the pattern. findings.failure_scenario: COST, two concrete ones. (1) `.coverage` is a binary SQLite file and CI now runs pytest-cov (.github/workflows/ci.yml:88): every local coverage run rewrites it, so `git status` is permanently dirty and any two branches that both ran coverage produce an unmergeable binary conflict. (2) test_client.py and test_services.py are root-level `test_*.py` that make live network calls (test_services.py:42 httpx, :87 redis, :126 supabase) — a bare `pytest` from the repo root collects them, which is part of why CLAUDE.md:441 has to warn that the default suite hangs. The documented workaround is `pytest tests/`; deleting these removes the need for the workaround.
findings.fix_sketch: `git rm --cached` all 16 (the .py probes are pure history — phase0_* was a 2026-05 luxury-SPA experiment long superseded by the _proof corpora), add `.coverage` and `/*.json` scratch patterns to .gitignore, and keep the ignore rules that are already there.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-verified independently. `git ls-files --error-unmatch` on all 16 paths succeeds for every one -- .coverage, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_luxury_test.json, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_result.json, full_response.json, parse_live.py, parse_luxury.py, parse_result.py, phase0_gucci.py, phase0_lv.py, phase0_lv_curl.py, phase0_test.py, session23_test_response.json, test_client.py, test_services.py, tmp_result.json, tmp_result2.json. .coverage is 53248 bytes on disk, matching the 53 KB claim, and CI does run coverage (`--cov=app --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=83` in the 'Run unit tests' step). The inert-ignore claim holds: .gitignore carries `/test_*.py` at :33 and `response_*.json` at :32 (the finding says :31 -- off by one), and `full_response.json` does not match `response_*.json` since the pattern anchors at the start of the basename. RAN THE COLLECTION PROOF: `python -m pytest --collect-only -q test_services.py test_client.py` collects 10 tests (test_openai, test_serper, test_redis, test_supabase, test_quick_comparison, test_health, test_rate_limit, test_quick_compare, test_image_compare, test_history), and pyproject's [tool.pytest.ini_options] sets no `testpaths`, so a bare root `pytest` does pick them up. test_services.py:40 (httpx), :81 (redis), :125 (supabase) are the live-call bodies (finding cites :42/:87/:126 -- within a couple of lines).

findings.title: 51 unused imports in the deployed backend, 9 of them in price_service including two whole modules
findings.claim: ruff F401 reports 51 unused imports under app/ (58 including scripts/); price_service.py alone carries 9, and line 38 imports two entire service modules — firecrawl_service and scrapedo_service — that the file never touches.
findings.evidence: `ruff check --select F401 app` → 51. price_service.py:26 extract_price, :27 extract_price_from_training_data, :32 search_product_prices + search_price_organic, :35 has_budget + record_usage + record_failure + record_success, :36 is_circuit_closed, :38 `from app.services import firecrawl_service, scrapedo_service`. Verified these are NOT deliberate re-exports: grepped every consumer for `from app.services.price_service import <sym>` and `price_service.<sym>` across app/, tests/ and scripts/ — zero hits for all nine. (The repo DOES use that re-export idiom deliberately and documents it at price_service.py:528-530 for SUPPLEMENT_KEYWORDS, so the pattern was checked rather than assumed.) The only firecrawl/scrapedo reference in the whole 15,622-line file is the import line itself; the real consumers are structured_comparison_service.py:61 (used at :1372, :1386, :1446) and source_router.py:619.
findings.failure_scenario: COST: the import list is how a reader (and every dependency-graph tool) infers what a module needs. price_service.py:35-36 advertises that it enforces the API budget circuit breaker — it does not; api_budget_service is enforced upstream. A maintainer trusting that import list will assume Firecrawl/Scrape.do budget checks happen here and skip adding them where they are actually needed. ruff's report-only tier already flags all 51, so the signal exists and is being discarded.
findings.fix_sketch: `ruff check --select F401 --fix app` is a safe autofix for all 51 (ruff marks them `[*]`). Optionally promote F401 from the report-only tier to the blocking tier for `app/` only, so it cannot re-accumulate.
findings.verify_evidence: Ran the tool myself. `python -m ruff check --select F401 app` -> 'Found 51 errors', `... app scripts` -> 'Found 58 errors' -- both counts exact. On price_service.py the concise output lists ELEVEN, not the nine the claim headline states: :26 extract_price, :27 extract_price_from_training_data, :32:41 search_product_prices, :32:64 search_price_organic, :35:5 has_budget, :35:17 record_usage, :35:31 record_failure, :35:47 record_success, :36:5 is_circuit_closed, :38:26 firecrawl_service, :38:45 scrapedo_service. The finding's own itemised evidence list contains all 11, so this is an arithmetic slip in the claim sentence, and it errs low -- I am UPGRADING the count, not the severity. Line 38 reads verbatim `from app.services import firecrawl_service, scrapedo_service`. Re-ran the deliberate-re-export counter-check myself for all 11 symbols (`from app.services.price_service import <sym>` and `price_service.<sym>` across app/, scripts/, tests/): zero hits for every one, while the documented genuine re-export precedent is confirmed at price_service.py:528-532 ('BC alias -- kept a derived union so structured_comparison_service's ... re-export at scs:1557 do not break'). So the pattern was correctly distinguished rather than assumed.

findings.title: 11 divergent hardcoded fetch timeouts across adapters; Bright Data's 20s exceeds the 15s price race with no pinning test
findings.claim: The 24 curl_cffi/httpx fetch sites spread over 11 adapter modules each carry their own hardcoded timeout constant (5s to 20s, none env-tunable), and brightdata_service._TIMEOUT = 20.0 is strictly greater than _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT = 15.0 — the one budget they all actually run under.
findings.evidence: Constants: algolia_service.py:148 _HTTP_TIMEOUT=8.0, noon_service.py:101 =8.0, unbxd_service.py:57 =8.0, woocommerce_service.py:64 _WOO_TIMEOUT=10, occ_service.py:76 _TIMEOUT=12, salla_service.py:58 =12, yotpo_service.py:61 =12, shopify_pdp_service.py:103 HTTP_TIMEOUT=12, magento_graphql_service.py:105 =12.0, price_service.py:633 PAGE_SCRAPE_TIMEOUT=5 / :639 BH_REGISTRY_CURL_TIMEOUT=10, brightdata_service.py:43 _TIMEOUT=20.0. The race budget is structured_comparison_service.py:1150 `_PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT", "15.0"))`. brightdata's value is applied at brightdata_service.py:116 `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_TIMEOUT)`, reached from serper_service.py:505-543 and :834-877 — i.e. from inside search_web/search_price_organic, which run inside the race. The repo already recognised this exact hazard for Serper and fixed it: serper_service.py:302 _serper_rotation_deadline defaults to 14.0 with the docstring "The default MUST stay strictly under that race budget (pinned by tests/test_serper_fail_fast.py)". No equivalent pin exists for Bright Data — tests/test_brightdata_fallback.py and tests/test_brightdata_budget_gate.py contain no timeout or race assertion.
findings.failure_scenario: CONCRETE: Serper key dead or budget-exhausted (both are the documented current state per CLAUDE.md's "Serper 403 STILL DEAD") → search_web falls through to bd_search_web → a Bright Data call with a 20s ceiling starts inside a 15s race. The race cancels at 15s, so a Bright Data response arriving at 16-20s is never usable: the fallback that was added to survive Serper depletion can only ever return in the sub-15s case, and the paid call made in the other case is billed and thrown away. Separately, lowering PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT via env silently strands every one of the 11 constants above it — the env knob does not reach them.
findings.fix_sketch: Derive every adapter timeout from one place: a module exposing `adapter_timeout(default)` clamped to `PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT` minus a margin, and set brightdata's ceiling below the race the way Serper's deadline already is. Add the brightdata analogue of tests/test_serper_fail_fast.py so the invariant is pinned rather than commented.
findings.verify_evidence: Every constant re-read at its cited line: algolia_service.py:148 _HTTP_TIMEOUT=8.0, noon_service.py:101 =8.0, unbxd_service.py:57 =8.0, woocommerce_service.py:64 _WOO_TIMEOUT=10, occ_service.py:76 _TIMEOUT=12, salla_service.py:58 =12, yotpo_service.py:61 =12, shopify_pdp_service.py:103 HTTP_TIMEOUT=12, magento_graphql_service.py:105 =12.0, price_service.py:633 PAGE_SCRAPE_TIMEOUT=5 and :639 BH_REGISTRY_CURL_TIMEOUT=10, brightdata_service.py:43 `_TIMEOUT = 20.0`. All are bare literals -- none reads os.getenv. The race budget is structured_comparison_service.py:1150 `_PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT", "15.0"))`, so 20.0 > 15.0 holds. Reachability re-derived by reading the call sites, not assumed: brightdata_service.py applies _TIMEOUT at `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_TIMEOUT)` inside _bd_post, and bd_search_web is invoked from serper_service search_web at :510/:521/:542 and from search_price_organic at :838/:846/:878 -- exactly the key-unavailable / budget-exhausted / non-200 branches, and search_price_organic is called inside _get_price at scs:6745, under the race. The asymmetry is the sharpest part and it verifies: tests/test_serper_fail_fast.py:167-173 is `test_rotation_deadline_default_is_under_the_price_race_budget` asserting `serper_service._serper_rotation_deadline() < _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT`, while my grep of tests/test_brightdata_fallback.py and tests/test_brightdata_budget_gate.py returns ZERO occurrences of timeout, race or _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT. One caveat that does not change severity: the fallback needs `_brightdata_enabled()` (brightdata_service.py:46-53 -- ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK plus both credentials), so the scenario is activation-conditional, which the finding's own 'fallback that was added to survive Serper depletion' framing already implies.

findings.title: Two contradictory Shopify variant-selection policies live in two modules
findings.claim: Shopify variant pricing is implemented twice with opposite rules: price_service._select_shopify_variant picks the 100 ml flagship (else the LARGEST bottle) and explicitly refuses the decant, while shopify_pdp_service.parse_shopify_pdp_json picks min(available variants) — the cheapest, i.e. the decant.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:14077-14123, docstring: "Bind the queried size to a specific Shopify variant instead of blindly pricing variants[0] (usually the smallest/cheapest -> a decant leak)"; :14118-14124 `flagship = [v for v, size, _a in valid if size == 100]` then `max(sized, key=...)` — "largest bottle, never the decant". shopify_pdp_service.py:435-441, Rule 1: `price_minor, chosen = min(priced_available, key=lambda pair: pair[0])`, `price_basis = "available_variant_min"`, commented "the floor of what a shopper can actually buy today". Both consume the same Shopify variant shape; the first serves the /products.json catalog channel (fetch_shopify_price :14396), the second the {pdp}.js channel (fetch_shopify_pdp_json :514). Also duplicated across the pair: money coercion — shopify_pdp_service.py:342 _to_minor / :388 _to_major are a private minor-unit parser alongside price_service.py:3169 parse_money. Both features are currently dark: variant_min_guard_enabled (price_service.py:4280) requires ENABLE_VARIANT_MIN_PRICE_GUARD and exact_gate_enabled; shopify_pdp_json_enabled (shopify_pdp_service.py:119) defaults OFF.
findings.failure_scenario: CONCRETE, on activation: a Gulf Shopify fragrance host offering 5 ml / 30 ml / 100 ml of one scent returns the 100 ml price through the catalog channel and the 5 ml decant price through the PDP-JSON channel. Which one a comparison shows depends only on which channel resolved first — so the same product can be priced ~20x apart run to run, and the pair-fairness reconciliation downstream (reconcile_pair_sizes :2006) is fed a size the other side never agreed to. CLAUDE.md's activation plan is an explicit seed-then-flip, so both flags are scheduled to go on.
findings.fix_sketch: Pick one policy and make the other call it. The flagship rule is the product-correct one for fragrances (it is the one with the decant-leak write-up behind it); shopify_pdp_service's min() rule should either take a size hint or be documented as availability-only and never used as the comparison price. Add a test asserting the two channels return the same variant for one fixture product before either flag is flipped.
findings.verify_evidence: CODE FACTS CONFIRMED, FLOW PREMISE REFUTED. Confirmed: price_service.py:14077-14124 `_select_shopify_variant` carries the quoted decant-leak docstring and picks `flagship = [v for v, size, _a in valid if size == 100]` else `max(sized, ...)` -- 'largest bottle, never the decant'; shopify_pdp_service.py:446 is `price_minor, chosen = min(priced_available, key=lambda pair: pair[0])` with `price_basis = "available_variant_min"` and the 'floor of what a shopper can actually buy today' comment. Two opposite rules do exist. REFUTED: the finding says these are two live comparison channels whose race order decides the price, so activation yields ~20x run-to-run divergence. I traced the wiring myself. The min() rule lives in `parse_shopify_pdp_json`, reachable only from `fetch_shopify_pdp_json` (:514) -- and my grep for both names across app/ and scripts/ returns ZERO hits; the only 47 references are in tests/test_shopify_pdp_json.py and tests/test_hostile_jsonld.py. The .js channel has no production caller, so flipping ENABLE_SHOPIFY_PDP_JSON adds one nowhere. The shopify_pdp_service entry that IS wired into the cascade is `fetch_ucp_json_price`, imported at price_service.py:13878 inside `_try_ucp_json_price`, and at shopify_pdp_service.py:1004-1007 it calls `ps._select_shopify_variant(...)` -- the SAME flagship policy -- under `ps.variant_min_guard_enabled()`. Its parser's docstring (:741-743) states outright 'Variant SELECTION is deliberately NOT done here -- that is the identity machinery's job'. price_service.py:4234 independently records that the .js adapter's _to_minor/_to_major 'are unreachable when their own flags are off'. Additional confirmation that the label cannot disambiguate downstream: `price_basis`/`available_variant_min` have zero consumers outside shopify_pdp_service.py. Residual genuine issue, hence P3 not REFUTED outright: two contradictory policies coexist in one repo and the entire .js channel (parse+fetch+_to_minor/_to_major, backed by a ~700-line test file) is unwired dead-on-arrival rather than merely dark-flagged -- a maintainer trap, not a pricing hazard.

findings.title: database_service exposes 4 zero-reference user-CRUD functions beside the live dual-client API
findings.claim: get_user_by_id :87, get_user_by_email :98, create_user :109 and update_user_subscription :123 — 50 lines — have zero references in app/, scripts/ or tests/.
findings.evidence: Whole-corpus reference count (app/, scripts/, tests/, docs/, migrations/, root) returns only the definition line for each of the four. The live user path goes through auth_service.py and the dual-client accessors CLAUDE.md:161 documents (get_user_supabase_client(token) for RLS vs get_admin_supabase_client() for service-role).
findings.failure_scenario: TRAP: these four sit at the top of the module, ahead of the dual-client accessors, and none of them takes an access_token. CLAUDE.md:161 states that user-facing DB functions MUST accept access_token so the query runs under RLS. A maintainer who reaches for create_user/get_user_by_email — the obvious names — gets a service-role query that bypasses row-level security on the users table, and no test catches it because the functions have no callers today.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete all four. If a user-lookup helper is wanted, add it with the mandatory access_token parameter next to the other RLS-aware accessors.
findings.verify_evidence: Independent reference count, since this is an absence claim. Word-boundary grep for each name across app/, scripts/ and tests/, excluding database_service.py itself: get_user_by_id 0, get_user_by_email 0, create_user 0, update_user_subscription 0. Definitions read at :87, :98, :109 and :123, ending at :135 -- 50 lines, matching. The RLS trap is verified in the bodies rather than inferred: all four open with `client = get_supabase_client()` and none accepts an access_token parameter, while CLAUDE.md:161 states 'Dual Supabase client: get_user_supabase_client(token) (anon+JWT, RLS) vs get_admin_supabase_client() (service-role). User-facing DB fns accept access_token. get_supabase_client() is deprecated alias for admin.' So reaching for create_user/get_user_by_email does yield a service-role query against the users table.

findings.title: 6 of the orchestrator's 39 back-compat wrappers are referenced by nothing at all
findings.claim: The block self-described at :2422-2425 as "Static method wrappers for backward compat (tests call svc._is_luxury_brand() etc.)" holds 39 pure pass-through methods; 34 have zero production call sites (tests only, which is the stated purpose) but 6 have zero references anywhere including tests.
findings.evidence: AST identified 39 methods whose whole body is a single call/return delegating to a module function. Production call sites (`self._<name>` under app/) are 0 for 38 of them; only _curl_fetch_html has one. Test call sites counted per wrapper — six are 0 in tests too: _is_accessory :2432, _is_high_value_query :2436, _detect_currency :2464, _extract_price_from_html :2581, _collect_retailer_ratings :2621, _format_review_search_results :7509 (12 lines total). Confirmed by whole-repo grep excluding the def line.
findings.failure_scenario: COST: the wrapper block is a second signature surface for 39 functions. Every parameter change to a delegated module function (e.g. extract_price_from_shopping gained shopping_region=) must be mirrored here or the wrapper silently drops the argument — the wrapper at :2578 does forward it, but nothing enforces that, and the six unreferenced wrappers prove the block is not maintained in step with either side. This is P3 rather than P2 because the block is deliberate and documented; only the six orphans are unambiguous waste.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the 6 unreferenced wrappers. For the other 33, have the tests import the module function directly — that removes a 220-line indirection layer that production stopped using.
findings.verify_evidence: Block header confirmed verbatim at structured_comparison_service.py:2422-2425: 'Static method wrappers for backward compat / (tests call svc._is_luxury_brand() etc.)'. My own AST pass over StructuredComparisonService using a strict rule (docstring-stripped body == one Return of a Call/Await) counts 37 pure delegators rather than the 39 claimed -- a stricter rule than the finding's, and the difference does not touch the six orphans. All six re-verified at the exact cited lines and confirmed unreferenced: _is_accessory :2432, _is_high_value_query :2436, _detect_currency :2464, _extract_price_from_html :2581, _collect_retailer_ratings :2621, _format_review_search_results :7509. Counted precisely rather than by substring -- a naive grep is misleading here because tests/test_accessory_reject_jsonld.py:57 and five siblings merely NAME test functions `test_is_accessory_*`; searching for actual call syntax (`.<name>(`) outside structured_comparison_service.py returns 0 for all six, and `self.<name>(` / `StructuredComparisonService.<name>(` inside the file returns 0 for all six. The control worked: the same method applied to _is_counterfeit_listing and _is_luxury_brand returns 13 and 13, so the six really are the outliers. P3 stands.

findings.title: Cron scripts import app.* with no sys.path bootstrap while CLAUDE.md documents them by path
findings.claim: Six scripts import app.* at module scope with no sys.path bootstrap (10 of 38 scripts do have one), and three are production cron entrypoints that CLAUDE.md documents in path form — which is the one invocation form that cannot work.
findings.evidence: No-bootstrap app importers: scripts/cron_reengagement.py (:23-25 `from app.services.database_service import get_admin_supabase_client` etc.), scripts/cron_expire_bonuses.py, scripts/cron_few_shot_rotation.py, scripts/ab_render_providers.py, scripts/diag_zyte_match.py, scripts/eval_persistence.py. Each ends in `if __name__ == "__main__"`. Reproduced the failure: with only the scripts/ directory on sys.path (exactly what `python scripts/cron_reengagement.py` produces) → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app'`. CLAUDE.md:170 documents it as "Daily cron `scripts/cron_reengagement.py`". The one cron with a committed invocation config gets it right: railway.warmer.json uses `python -m scripts.cron_warm_price_cache`, the module form, which does work.
findings.failure_scenario: CONCRETE: whoever schedules the re-engagement cron follows CLAUDE.md:170 literally and runs `python scripts/cron_reengagement.py`. It dies instantly on ModuleNotFoundError. Because the job is gated behind ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES and pushes are best-effort, a cron that never runs looks identical to a cron whose detectors found nobody — the failure is silent until someone asks why no re-engagement pushes ever went out.
findings.fix_sketch: Either add the 2-line `sys.path.insert` bootstrap the other 10 scripts use, or change CLAUDE.md:170 and the sibling cron docs to the `python -m scripts.<name>` form that railway.warmer.json already proves correct. The second is better — it matches the one invocation that is actually committed anywhere.
findings.verify_evidence: REPRODUCED. `subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'scripts/cron_reengagement.py'], cwd=repo_root, env without PYTHONPATH)` exits rc=1 with 'File "...\\scripts\\cron_reengagement.py", line 23, in <module> / from app.services.database_service import get_admin_supabase_client / ModuleNotFoundError: No module named app' -- the exact line and error claimed. My own AST enumeration over all 38 scripts (module-scope app.* import AND no sys.path.insert/append in source) returns precisely the six named: ab_render_providers.py, cron_expire_bonuses.py, cron_few_shot_rotation.py, cron_reengagement.py, diag_zyte_match.py, eval_persistence.py. `grep -l 'sys.path.insert|sys.path.append' scripts/*.py` = 10, matching the '10 of 38' figure. CLAUDE.md:170 documents it in path form verbatim ('Daily cron `scripts/cron_reengagement.py`'), and railway.warmer.json's startCommand is `python -m scripts.cron_warm_price_cache`, the working module form. ONE OVERSTATEMENT: 'three are production cron entrypoints that CLAUDE.md documents in path form' -- only cron_reengagement.py is documented with the `scripts/` path; cron_expire_bonuses.py appears at CLAUDE.md:251 as a bare filename, and cron_few_shot_rotation.py does not appear in CLAUDE.md at all. The reproduced defect and its doc citation both stand.

findings.title: .gitignore's ".qa-*/ NEVER track" comment claims a fail-closed guarantee that 7 tracked files disprove
findings.claim: The .qa-*/ ignore rule carries a comment stating that gitignoring "fail-closes" a token-leak vector flagged by a prior branch review, but seven files under .qa-bh-sourcing/ and .qa-bias-rerun/ are still tracked — the rule cannot untrack what was already committed.
findings.evidence: .gitignore:59-63 reads "Session QA / recon / agent scratch. NEVER track — recon dumps can contain live tokens (e.g. .qa-bh-sourcing/_f3_nasser_main.js carries a scraped guest token). Whole-branch review #4 (bh-source-intelligence) flagged this as a latent git-add-A leak vector; gitignoring fail-closes it." `git ls-files .qa-bh-sourcing .qa-bias-rerun` returns 7 paths: _verify_bolo.py, _verify_nasser.py, _partial_assembly_mock_harness.py, _render_capability_bh_retailers.py, _render_dump_one.py, _sephora_provider_test.py, bias_matrix_24.json. Scanned all seven for Bearer/JWT/api_key/token patterns — clean, and the specifically-named leaky file _f3_nasser_main.js is NOT tracked, so no live secret is exposed today.
findings.failure_scenario: COST: the status claim is wrong, and it is the kind of claim someone relies on. A reviewer reading .gitignore:62 concludes the .qa-* surface is closed and stops checking; the next recon dump written into an ALREADY-TRACKED .qa-* directory is picked up by `git add -A` regardless of the ignore rule, which is precisely the vector the comment says was closed. Reported because the ground rules call for documented items whose status claim is wrong.
findings.fix_sketch: `git rm --cached -r .qa-bh-sourcing .qa-bias-rerun` (the 7 files are session scratch with no consumer), then the comment's claim becomes true. Amend the comment to note that ignore rules do not untrack.
findings.verify_evidence: known_item STATUS CLAIM VERIFIED AS WRONG, which is what the ground rules ask of a documented item. .gitignore:59-63 reads verbatim 'Session QA / recon / agent scratch. NEVER track -- recon dumps can contain live tokens (e.g. .qa-bh-sourcing/_f3_nasser_main.js carries a scraped guest token). Whole-branch review #4 (bh-source-intelligence) flagged this as a latent git-add-A leak vector; gitignoring fail-closes it.' with the rule `.qa-*/` at :63. I ran the check myself: `git ls-files .qa-bh-sourcing .qa-bias-rerun` returns exactly the 7 paths claimed -- .qa-bh-sourcing/{_verify_bolo.py,_verify_nasser.py} and .qa-bias-rerun/{_partial_assembly_mock_harness.py,_render_capability_bh_retailers.py,_render_dump_one.py,_sephora_provider_test.py,bias_matrix_24.json}. The specifically-named leaky file is confirmed NOT tracked: `git ls-files .qa-bh-sourcing/_f3_nasser_main.js` returns empty, and `ls .qa-bh-sourcing/` shows only the two tracked .py probes on disk. So no live secret is exposed today and the finding correctly says so -- what is false is the comment's fail-closed guarantee, since gitignore never untracks an already-committed path and `git add -A` will still pick up new files written into those two tracked directories.

findings.title: The openai import-bomb note points at openai_service.py:20; the client is built at :27
findings.claim: The documented import-time-client trap is still live (reproduced), but both places that record it cite openai_service.py:20, and the AsyncOpenAI construction is at line 27.
findings.evidence: Reproduced at HEAD with OPENAI_API_KEY unset: `import app.services.openai_service` → `OpenAIError: The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable`. The construction is app/services/openai_service.py:27 `client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=provider_base_url(), timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=30.0))`; line 20 is inside the `from app.services.model_config import (...)` block. Both records are stale the same way: requirements.in:7 "app/services/openai_service.py:20 builds AsyncOpenAI at module import" and CLAUDE.md:441 "Related: `openai_service.py:20` builds `AsyncOpenAI` at module import". findings.failure_scenario: COST: a reader following the note opens line 20, sees an import of model_config, and either concludes the note is wrong or that the trap was already fixed. findings.title: One test file carries a UTF-8 BOM that breaks non-import-based tooling
findings.claim: tests/test_subtype_spec_reconciliation.py is the only .py file in the repo that starts with a UTF-8 BOM, which any tool reading it as plain utf-8 (rather than utf-8-sig) fails to parse.
findings.evidence: Byte scan over every tracked .py file: exactly one hit (EF BB BF at offset 0). `ast.parse` on the file read with encoding="utf-8" → `SyntaxError: invalid non-printable character U+FEFF (line 1)`. Python's own import machinery and py_compile use utf-8-sig, so pytest collection and .githooks/pre-commit's py_compile stanza are unaffected — this only bites tools that open the file themselves. Note requirements.in and requirements-dev.in also carry a BOM; pip and uv decode those with BOM handling, so they are fine.
findings.failure_scenario: COST: any repo-wide AST pass silently drops this file. My own dead-code scan hit it and reported PARSE FAIL — meaning a coverage-driven audit of this test file's contents is invisible to exactly the kind of whole-tree tooling the repo's audits depend on. The failure is silent-by-default (a scan that skips one file still exits 0).
findings.fix_sketch: Strip the BOM (`python -c "p='tests/test_subtype_spec_reconciliation.py'; s=open(p,encoding='utf-8-sig').read(); open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)"`), and add a BOM check to .githooks/pre-commit beside the existing py_compile stanza.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-ran the byte scan over the git index rather than the filesystem: iterating `git ls-files '*.py'` (723 tracked .py files) and reading the first 3 bytes of each, EXACTLY ONE carries EF BB BF -- tests/test_subtype_spec_reconciliation.py. Then reproduced both halves of the parse claim in one process: `ast.parse(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read())` raises 'SyntaxError: invalid non-printable character U+FEFF (line 1)', while `ast.parse(open(p, encoding='utf-8-sig').read())` succeeds. The 'only .py in the repo' scope is confirmed against tracked files (backend/ and SmartCompareApp/ included in the ls-files sweep). The requirements.in / requirements-dev.in BOMs are also real -- both files' first line renders with a leading U+FEFF when read as utf-8 -- and the finding is right that pip/uv decode those with BOM handling.
